scope: npm run test:mutation (stryker.config.json's src/-scoped run) -- not npm run test:mutation:scripts, which carries no ignorePatterns at all and reads features/** from the live tree in its own tests

allow.argument: Tracked, and therefore copied into Stryker's sandbox, but never mutated (mutate is src/**) and consulted by no test, build, or lint config; a fixed filename can never itself become a test glob match. Verified by grepping vite.config.ts, vitest.scripts.config.ts, src/test-setup.ts, fast-check-stryker-seed.ts and both Stryker configs for a live (non-comment) reference, plus scanning scripts/ test files for a readFileSync of the real CLAUDE.md rather than a throwaway mkdtempSync fixture -- agent-doc-check's and reference-check's own tests, which do read CLAUDE.md in production, build a temp repo per case.
Same category and same verification as CLAUDE.md: tracked but never mutated (mutate is src/**), and consulted by no test, build, or lint config.

Not mutated (mutate is src/**); no script or config in vite.config.ts, the vitest.*.config.ts files, or either Stryker config references Vale, and there is no npm run script that invokes it -- the prose linter is run by hand.

Not mutated (mutate is src/**); tracked and copied into the sandbox but nothing there consults it -- oxlint is referenced by neither vite.config.ts, vitest.scripts.config.ts, src/test-setup.ts, fast-check-stryker-seed.ts nor either Stryker config.

absent.reason: Decides the src/ mutation run's own mutate/ignorePatterns scope; editing it must re-arm the gate, the same reasoning that keeps mutation-invariance.config.json itself absent.
Decides the scripts/ mutation run's scope; same re-arming reasoning as stryker.config.json.
Defines vitest's sharedExclude, which is what makes the vitest-exclude tier sound in the first place; editing it can change what the gate sees.
A separate vitest project outside stryker.config.json's mutate scope, but its own exclude list can change what a *.browser.test.ts run covers.
Configures the scripts/ vitest project; can change what a scripts/ test collects, and therefore what a scripts/-scoped mutant is killed by.
Carries every npm script this gate and every other gate run through; editing it can change what runs.
Pins the dependency tree Stryker's sandbox installs from.
The project-reference root; changing it can change what `tsc -b` includes.
Its `include` is ["src", "features", "perf"] -- the reason a features/**-only diff still moves `npm run build`.
Part of the same project-reference graph as tsconfig.json.
Its `include` is scripts/, governing what the scripts/ vitest project (and therefore the scripts/ mutation run) compiles.

Ruled absent by inventory rather than by a structural coupling to rules/**: never mutated, read by no test, consulted by nothing inside the sandbox -- but no diff has yet been blocked by it alone, so it is left out on the same .prettierignore ground rather than allowlisted.
patch-package output applied at postinstall; can change installed dependency behavior the sandbox runs against.
Governs what is tracked and therefore copied into Stryker's sandbox; deliberately left out of the vitest/stryker-exclude reasoning that covers ideas/**, .claude/** and rules/**/rule-tests/**.
Left absent on the same ground as sgconfig.yml -- an allowlist should carry only what has been argued and needed, and no diff has yet been blocked by it alone.
Stryker's own mutate scope; obviously moves the score.
The scripts/ mutation run's own mutate scope; moves the scripts/ score, and some scripts/ tests read features/** from the live tree.
Included in tsconfig.app.json's build scope.
Static assets served by the built app; never argued safe.
Decides this gate's own scope; editing it must re-arm the gate, exactly as stryker.config.json does.
Backs this gate's own config validation; editing it must re-arm the gate for the same reason as the config file itself.
